w: A 140-room Georgian Revival hotel five miles from Rocky Mountain National Park's entrance, with views over Lake Estes, the Rockies and Longs Peak, and a reputation as one of America's most haunted hotels. In May 2025 it changed hands again, bought by a public-private partnership for roughly 400 million dollars.
s: Georgian Revival hotel ranked among America's most haunted

w: Imogene Green MacPherson homesteaded this site in 1903 and ran it as Moraine Park Lodge until her 1928 death and the Park Service's 1931 purchase. The stone-and-log museum and its 1935 amphitheater, built by the Civilian Conservation Corps, sit in a glaciated meadow between two moraines.
s: 1920s homestead lodge turned NPS Rustic museum
_facts: Imogene Green MacPherson homesteaded the site ("Hillcrest") in 1903 and opened the lodge in 1905
Built as Moraine Park Lodge in 1923; NPS purchased it in 1931 and razed surrounding cabins
1935 amphitheater built by the Civilian Conservation Corps in NPS Rustic style
Sits in Moraine Park, a glaciated meadow between two moraines

w: Editor William Allen White bought an 1887 cabin near Estes Park in 1912, his summer home until his 1944 death. Guests included Clarence Darrow, William Jennings Bryan, Jane Addams and Chief Justice Charles Evans Hughes. The Park Service acquired it in 1972, rehabilitating it in 1976 for artists-in-residence.
s: Editor's mountain retreat that hosted Darrow and Addams
_facts: William Allen White bought an 1887 cabin near Estes Park in 1912, summer home until his 1944 death
Guests included Clarence Darrow, William Jennings Bryan, Jane Addams, Charles Evans Hughes
First property nominated to the NRHP from Rocky Mountain National Park
NPS acquired it in 1972; rehabilitated 1976 for an artists-in-residence program

w: The Park Theatre opened in downtown Estes Park in 1913 and has run ever since, making it the oldest continuously operating cinema in the western United States - a single-screen theatre still showing films in the same building more than a hundred years after its marquee first lit up.
s: Oldest running cinema in the western US, since 1913
_facts: Opened in 1913 in downtown Estes Park
Oldest operating movie theater in the western United States
